expectations.description: Warns against adding modifications purely to improve fit (MI-chasing)
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'don't just add those modifications and report the improved model as if nothing changed' and dedicates a section to 'The MI-chasing problem,' explaining why acting post-hoc without theory corrupts a confirmatory analysis.

expectations.description: Uses or invokes the concept of 'capitalization on chance' or 'overfit' or 'sample-specific'
expectations.evidence: Uses all three: 'capitalizing on chance,' 'This is overfit — a model increasingly tailored to sample-specific quirks,' and references sample-specific noise throughout.

expectations.description: Recommends substantive justification for any modification (e.g., similar item wording, method effects)
expectations.evidence: Provides explicit examples of substantively justified correlated residuals (nearly identical wording, reverse-worded items, adjacent administration, longitudinal same-indicator) and states 'The MI value alone is not a rationale.'

expectations.description: Recommends cross-validation, replication, or holdout sample if modifications are made
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states 'Cross-validate. Run the respecified model on a holdout sample (random split), or better, collect a replication sample.'

expectations.description: States that the resulting model should be characterized as exploratory/respecified, not confirmatory
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section 'You are no longer doing CFA' explains this directly: 'the analysis is exploratory respecification, not confirmatory factor analysis.' Also states final model should be 'labeled as a respecified or exploratory model.'

expectations.description: Suggests examining standardized residuals to understand WHERE the model misfits, not just global indices
expectations.evidence: Full section 'Before reaching for MIs, inspect where the model misfits' recommends `residuals(fit, type = 'standardized')` with R code and explains how large standardized residuals flag specific item pairs more usefully than global indices.

expectations.description: Does not endorse adding the MIs without any caveats
expectations.evidence: The response never endorses adding the modifications; it warns against the approach throughout and, when describing conditions under which modifications are defensible, imposes multiple requirements (substantive rationale, documentation, cross-validation, honest characterization).
